skeleton.brief: Introduce the common circular water cycle drawing
Explain evaporation mostly from oceans
Describe condensation forming clouds around dust and salt

narration.text: Every school draws the water cycle as a circle, and the circle is right.

slot_stat.heading: The Water Cycle
bullets: A familiar circular drawing in science classes

narration.text: Start with evaporation. About eighty-six percent of the water that enters the atmosphere comes off the ocean, not off lakes and rivers.

narration.text: That vapour rises, cools and condenses into cloud droplets around specks of dust and salt. Without those specks the air would just stay humid.

narration.text: Then precipitation, and here is the imbalance: about seventy-eight percent of rain falls back onto the ocean it came from. Only the remainder reaches land at all.
On land the water splits three ways. Some runs off into rivers, some soaks into the soil for plants, and some sinks into groundwater that may not see the surface for a thousand years.

asset_request.guidance: A natural river flowing through a forest or green landscape, no people or animals.

narration.text: And then collection, back to the ocean, and the loop starts again.
The cycle takes about nine days for a single molecule in the atmosphere, and up to ten thousand years for one that ends up in deep groundwater.

narration.text: The atmosphere is not a fog that thins out. It is five distinct layers.

slot_stat.heading: 5 Distinct Layers
bullets: Separated by temperature changes

narration.text: The troposphere is the bottom twelve kilometres, where all the weather is and where it gets colder the higher you go. Everything you have ever seen happen in the sky happened here.

asset_request.guidance: A clear photo showing clouds and weather activity in the lower atmosphere.

narration.text: Above it the stratosphere runs to about fifty kilometres, and here the temperature goes back up, because the ozone layer is absorbing ultraviolet. That warm-on-top arrangement is why it does not mix, and why airliners fly in the bottom of it.
The mesosphere, to about eighty-five kilometres, is where meteors burn up. It is the coldest place in the atmosphere, around minus ninety.

narration.text: Compound interest is the most oversold idea in personal finance, and it is also entirely real.

slot_quote.heading: Compound interest is the most oversold idea in personal finance, and it is also entirely real.
bullets: — anonymous personal finance expert

narration.text: The formula is A equals P times one plus r over n, raised to n times t. P is what you put in, r is the annual rate, n is how often it compounds, t is years.
Put in ten thousand at seven percent. After one year you have ten thousand seven hundred, which is not interesting.
After ten years you have nineteen thousand seven hundred.
After thirty years you have seventy-six thousand.
Growth is exponential, so the curve is almost flat for years and then bends upward hard, and almost all of the money arrives in the last third of the time.

cases.title: Why does a squared plus b squared equal c squared

skeleton.brief: Introduce Pythagoras and question its proof
State the Pythagorean theorem with squares on triangle sides
Draw four triangles inside a large square of side a plus b
Show tilted square of side c inside the large square
Rearrange triangles to reveal squares of sides a and b
Compare leftover areas to prove c² = a² + b²
Emphasize the proof comes from rearranging triangles
what the result lets you do

narration.text: Here is a claim worth doubting — until you see it.
We claim the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares on the legs. This fundamental relation holds for any right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c.

slot_main.heading: Pythagoras' theorem
bullets: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 for right triangle

narration.text: Start with a large square of side a plus b. Inside it, place four copies of the right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c. This arrangement leaves a tilted square of side c in the center. Highlight the tilted square of side c formed inside the large square by the four triangles. This square's area is c squared, which we want to relate to the other parts. Rearrange the four triangles inside the same large square to reveal two smaller squares of sides a and b. These squares represent the areas a squared and b squared. Compare the leftover areas in both arrangements. Since the large square and four triangles are unchanged, the leftover areas must be equal, proving c squared equals a squared plus b squared.

The two leftover areas must match because the outer square and four triangles are the same in both arrangements. This equality confirms the Pythagorean relation c squared equals a squared plus b squared.

This proof shows that the Pythagorean theorem isn't just a formula to memorize. It's a natural result of rearranging shapes. This lets you find unknown sides and understand the deep link between geometry and algebra.

cases.title: What a half life really means

skeleton.brief: Explain what a half life really means, correcting a common misconception
Introduce carbon fourteen and its half life duration
Show how the quantity halves over successive half lives
Explain the decay curve never reaches zero, it halves forever
Present the decay equation relating half life and decay constant
Emphasize that atoms do not age and decay probability is constant
Explain why this memoryless property makes dating possible
The remaining proportion acts as a reliable clock for dating

narration.text: A half life is not how long something lasts. It is how long it takes for half of what is there to go.
Carbon fourteen is a radioactive isotope with a half life of about five thousand seven hundred and thirty years. This means it takes that long for half of a sample to decay.

slot_term.definition: A radioactive isotope of carbon used in dating ancient materials, with a half life of 5,730 years.
slot_term.caption: Also called radiocarbon
slot_term.heading: Carbon Fourteen

narration.text: Starting with one kilogram, after one half life you have half a kilogram left, after two half lives a quarter, and after three just an eighth.
The decay curve never reaches zero. It keeps halving forever, getting closer and closer but never quite disappearing.

slot_plot.heading: Radioactive Decay Curve
slot_plot.caption: Quantity halves continuously but never reaches zero

narration.text: The decay equation is N equals N nought times e to the minus lambda t, where lambda is the decay constant related to the half life.
A carbon fourteen atom does not age. Its chance to decay is the same whether it’s five thousand years old or freshly formed. There is no memory in it.

slot_quote.heading: "A carbon fourteen atom that has sat in a bone for five thousand years is exactly as likely to decay in the next second as one made this morning."
bullets: — Explainer on radioactive decay

narration.text: This memoryless property is why radiocarbon dating works. The remaining proportion acts as a reliable clock, unaffected by the sample’s history.
